correctness.rationale: The counting lower bound is immediate because a length-three word has at most three distinct length-two deletion descendants. For odd q, the cited quadratic-leave theorem yields a triangle decomposition of K_q minus C_q when q is 3 mod 6 (q>=9), or K_q minus C_{q-1} plus an isolated point when q is 1 or 5 mod 6. Two opposite orderings of each triangle cover both directions of its three edges; words of the form (a,b,a) cover one loop and both directions of a leave edge. The block counts give exactly ceil(q^2/3). q=3 is checked directly.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Xie--Sun--Ge give D(q,3,1)=(1+o(1))q^2/3 through their fixed-(n,R) theorem, which is broader in n,R but weaker than exact equality at finite odd q. Colbourn--Rosa is broader as a design-existence theorem, but its conclusion alone is not the coding parameter statement until combined with the deletion-ball translation given here.

value.rationale: D(q,3,1) is the first nontrivial short-block deletion-covering parameter associated with the 2026 large-alphabet program. Exact attainment of the elementary lower bound on every odd alphabet is a natural infinite-family refinement of the known asymptotic statement, and the construction exposes a reusable bridge from partial triple-system leaves to synchronization covering codes rather than merely recomputing a finite table.
